title: Pedro de Sintra names the mountains
description: The Portuguese explorer maps the coast and calls its highlands Serra Lyoa, the Lion Mountains, which becomes the country's name.

title: Province of Freedom settlement
description: London abolitionists led by Granville Sharp land some 400 freed 'Black Poor' bought from a Temne king; fever and local hostility wipe the settlement out within two years.

title: Freetown founded
description: More than a thousand Black Loyalists resettled from Nova Scotia found the Sierra Leone Company's town, parent of the Krio people.

title: Jamaican Maroons arrive
description: Some 550 Maroons deported after revolt in Jamaica help crush a Nova Scotian rising and then settle, another strand in the Krio mix.

title: Sierra Leone becomes a crown colony
description: Britain takes over the settlement as a base for its squadron against the slave ships, and liberated Africans from across West Africa pour in.

title: Protectorate proclaimed over the interior
description: Britain extends its rule from the Krio coast over the Mende and Temne interior, setting the country's two-tier colonial order.

title: Hut Tax War
description: Bai Bureh of the Temne and Mende chiefs rise against the new house tax in a war that costs the protectorate hundreds of lives before it is beaten down.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Sierra Leone becomes independent with Milton Margai as prime minister.

title: Albert Margai succeeds his brother
description: Milton Margai dies and his brother takes over, drifting toward one-party rule and losing the party's northern support.

title: Disputed election and two coups
description: Siaka Stevens wins the vote but the army chief seizes power before he is sworn in, then junior officers topple both and rule through a junta.

title: Sergeants' coup restores Stevens
description: Rank-and-file soldiers overthrow the junta and hand the premiership to Stevens, who then holds power for seventeen years.

title: Sierra Leone becomes a republic
description: Days after a failed army coup, a republican constitution makes Stevens the first president and Guinea's troops fly in to secure him.

title: One-party state
description: A referendum makes Stevens's All People's Congress the only legal party; student protests are answered with shooting.

title: Momoh succeeds Stevens
description: The ailing president hands over to his army chief Joseph Momoh, under whom the economy and the state decay.

title: Civil war begins
description: Foday Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front crosses from Liberia and seizes border villages, opening eleven years of war.

title: Young officers' coup
description: Unpaid frontline soldiers march on the capital and install 25-year-old Captain Valentine Strasser at the head of a junta.

title: Kabbah elected amid the war
description: Voters defy rebel mutilations to elect Ahmad Tejan Kabbah president under a new multiparty constitution.

title: AFRC coup
description: Major Johnny Paul Koroma's soldiers break open the prisons, chase Kabbah into Guinea and invite the RUF into government.

title: ECOMOG restores Kabbah
description: Nigerian-led West African troops storm the capital and drive the AFRC-RUF junta back into the bush.

title: Assault on Freetown
description: Rebels storm into the capital and spend weeks burning, amputating and killing through its eastern suburbs before ECOMOG fights them out.

title: Lomé Peace Agreement
description: Kabbah signs away cabinet seats and an amnesty to Sankoh for a peace the RUF's troops do not keep.

title: British intervene
description: As the RUF advances again and takes peacekeepers hostage, British paratroops secure Freetown's airport and turn the war.

title: War declared over
description: With disarmament complete, Kabbah declares the war over; it has killed some 50,000 and displaced half the country.

title: Special Court set up
description: A UN-backed court begins work to try those most responsible for the war, and later convicts Liberia's Charles Taylor.

title: Ebola epidemic
description: The West African outbreak crosses from Guinea into Kailahun and kills nearly 4,000 Sierra Leoneans before the government declares victory.
